doc.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022

title: Passing on what he learns, and buying instruments today
summary: He always shares discoveries, illustrated by buying instruments cheaply at a closing music store and his email list.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Wow that’s a great anecdote. Was there a point that you can recall now where you started to pass on to other people what you had — you know this light that came on for you and then you could pass it on?

I’ve always been that way. You know if I find something that seems to work, the first thing I want to do is call my friend and tell him. You know or email somebody. Today I bought some instruments, there’s a little music store downtown right across from the post office. And at 11:00 today they were selling everything in the store and they’re going to go into just teaching, and fifty dollars for however much you can carry out. So I went in, © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

I was about the twentieth person to get in there. So I picked up a flute, a Selmer saxophone, a snare drum, something else, something else stuffed in my pocked, a mute, and this, that and the other, for fifty dollars. I checked it out and walked the half a block to my car and put it in the trunk, but on my way walking over there I was already thinking about it, going home and emailing my friends. There were some guitars left on the walls, you know? Maybe they’d like to come and buy a guitar for fifty dollars. Yes, as soon as I learn something I’m passing it on. So I’ve never been a hoarder in that respect at all. Yeah I’m always passing stuff on. As a matter of fact I have an email list which I probably ought to put you on. And some people say, “Jamey, gosh, you send too many emails.” I say, “Well then block me” you know. But I don’t send anything out unless I feel it’s important.
